items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Alex ... had heard about Henri "Red" Allen but never seen a photo of him.

ctx.x: One of the first young French jazz musicians that I made acquaintance with was a tenor player named Alex Combelle. Exactly how we met, I cannot recall, but I remember that Alex Combelle used to come to my room in the Hotel Eden and ask me about many musicians in the States and especially about ones around New York. Alex spoke English quite well. All that I knew to say in French was : 'bonjour, monsoir' and 'oui' (wee).

I had a photograph album with some photos of different musicians I had worked with and showed them to Alex. He knew about quite a few of them and besides Armstrong, he had heard about Henri "Red" Allen but never seen a photo of him. He pointed to Red's photo and asked me who he was. I told him it was Red Allen. His comment was: Hum, funny face!

I also had a nice collection of records mostly Armstrongs and a portable phonograph and Alex enjoyed listening to the records he had not heard before. I also remember that I caught a cold once and told Alex that I would like to have something to cure it but I didn't know what to ask in French. So he brought me some pills and when I saw them, they were white and about the size of a beer bottle cap and I knew I could not swallow something the size of that. But Alex told me to take one, put it in my mouth, then take…
